title: introduce-weighted-headroom-harmonizer-and-utilization-sentry-for-dedicated-fleet
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently use a single headroom target per pool which causes oscillation when tenants with bursty traffic compete for transient capacity. This PR introduces two coordinated features: a weighted headroom harmonizer (an autoscaler policy that allocates headroom proportionally to tenant importance and observed tail-utilization) and an independent utilization sentry service that produces smoothed per-tenant utilization fingerprints for the harmonizer to consume. Key benefits: smoother scaling decisions, fewer micro-scale provisioning churns, improved throughput guarantees during transient spikes, and clearer telemetry for SLA debugging. Design summary: 1) Weighted Headroom Harmonizer: policy evaluates per-tenant effective weight = config.weight * max(1, percentile_util/target_util); desired_headroom = base_headroom * normalized_weight; uses multi-window smoothing (5s, 30s, 5m) to avoid reacting to short spikes; respects pool-level max_headroom_pct and cluster budget constraints; supports manual overrides and canary tiers. 2) Utilization Sentry: lightweight collector deployed per-pool that computes HDR sketches and percentile deltas on rolling windows and exports aggregated 50/90/99 utilization and burstiness score to the orchestrator via a compact protobuf. It also emits change-points to accelerate harmonizer when a true workload shift is detected. Compatibility and safety: harmonizer is opt-in per-pool and defaults to passthrough behavior; when enabled, autoscaler fallback rules ensure we never reduce reserved capacity below existing commitments; the harmonizer can be configured with conservative gain and cooldown settings for gradual rollout. Telemetry and observability: new metrics: redwood.harmonizer.effective_weight, redwood.harmonizer.desired_headroom_pct, redwood.sentry.burstiness_score, redwood.sentry.delta_pctiles, and event logs for change-point triggers. Dashboard: added a harmonizer panel to Dedicated -> Pools showing headroom allocation per-tenant and predicted provisioning delta. Tests and validation: unit tests for weight normalization, simulated cluster-level integration tests with synthetic tenants (steady, periodic burst, random microbursts), and two-night canary on a small dedicated pool. Performance: sentry uses O(1) per-request amortized CPU and keeps memory at <2MB per-pool by using compact sketches; harmonizer computation runs on the control-plane cadence (default 5s) and is horizontally sharded. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind pool config.enable_weighted_headroom; rollout plan: 1) dry-run mode (0%) with metrics only; 2) canary on non-critical dedicated pools for 48-72h; 3) gradual ramp to 25/50/100% across regions in 1-2 weeks if there are no regressions. Related work items: ENG-2489, ENG-2620; support follow-up SUP-342. Implementation notes: avoid tight coupling with the existing reservation ledger; harmonizer emits desired headroom signals that the existing provisioner reconciler consumes; added idempotent tests to ensure reconciler tolerates transient conflicting signals. Security and perf review: no new network surface besides internal control plane RPCs; protobuf message is versioned. Rollback: harmonizer supports immediate disable flag and a fast-fail-safe which falls back to legacy allocation on mismatch thresholds. Checklist: [x] design doc; [x] unit tests; [x] e2e simulations; [x] telemetry dashboards; [x] canary run configured; [x] docs. Potential follow-ups: integrate tenant-priority SLA scores into weight calculation; add machine-learning based burst predictors as an optional plugin.
